Title: A hack for good mental health
NewsSummary: Hackathon brings together students to design solutions for mental wellbeing
NewsContent:
AKU's first-ever mental health hackathon empowered students to design solutions to address individual and societal challenges affecting mental health and wellbeing. 

Mental health conditions affect a staggering one in four people at some time in their lives. According to some estimates, between 35-50 percent of people with severe mental health disorders receive no treatment in the global North. The figure balloons up to 85 percent in the global South. 

The Student Mental Health Hackathon took place as a virtual, multi-day event for AKU students, trainees and medical residents from Africa, Asia and Europe. Also participating were other universities and partners, mental health specialists, innovation and entrepreneurship professionals, and champions of student experience. 

The aim was to share ideas and solve problems that are pertinent to student mental health and wellbeing. The Hackathon invited teams to model their solutions within AKU's integrated mental health framework.

About 300 students engaged in the event, roughly 10 percent of AKU's student population. "We were not only in a competition but in a learning space," said one of the participants.

Ten teams presented proposed innovations to a panel of judges with the top three teams winning iPads for each team member. Seven teams have been selected to present their ideas to the Brain and Mind Institute's Implementation Science Team. 

Participants were enthusiastic about the experience. "This is something I never thought I could do at Med School," commented one person. For another, it was "a life-changing experience."

Hackathon teams wishing to pursue their innovation ideas have been encouraged to proceed to incubation through the hackathon's partnerships with Critical Creative Innovative Thinking (CCIT) forum, Ryerson University and Accelerate Prosperity. 

The Brain and Mind Institute hosted the Hackathon in partnership with CCIT and Student Affairs and Services.
